new_statements.quote: Sobre los rasgos prosódicos de la variedad afirma que el acento es la unidad prosódica distintiva que se realiza en el pico silábico; y en palabras de más de cuatro sílabas, plantea que puede haber hasta dos acentos, unos principal y uno secundario. Igual que Headland y Headland (1976) y Casilimas (1995), como se indicó, Calvete (1995) señala que la variedad de Chaparral cuenta con el rasgo prosódico de acentuación con una función distintiva, pero a diferencia de las demás investigaciones, no menciona la existencia de la nasalidad.
new_statements.translation: On the prosodic features of the variety he states that stress is the distinctive prosodic unit, realised on the syllable peak; and in words of more than four syllables he proposes that there may be up to two stresses, one primary and one secondary. Like Headland & Headland (1976) and Casilimas (1995), as noted, Calvete (1995) indicates that the Chaparral variety has the prosodic feature of accentuation with a distinctive function, but unlike the other studies he does not mention the existence of nasality.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is contrastive (distinctive) in the Chaparral/Casanare (eastern, Barro Negro) variety; no placement rule is reported, so position must be treated as lexically specified until Calvete 1995 itself is read. Words longer than four syllables may carry two stresses.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Up to two stresses, one primary and one secondary, in words of more than four syllables (Calvete 1995 per Gómez Vargas 2022 p. 21).
new_statements.exceptions: None reported; the summary is a paraphrase without examples.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word; stress realised on the syllable peak. Report is a second-hand paraphrase in a literature review; the underlying thesis (Chaparral, Hato Corozal, Casanare) is not accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: Barro Negro Tunebo [tbn] = the eastern U'wa of Casanare (Barro Negro, Tabías, San Lope; municipios Sácama, Hato Corozal/Chaparral, Támara), called 'Chaparral-Barronegro -u'wa oriental-' by Gómez Vargas 2022 (pp. 12, 24, after Gómez 2016 and Ethnologue) and the 'Barronegro' dialect by Headland & Headland 1976. The second-hand statement (Calvete 1995) describes the Chaparral (Hato Corozal, Casanare) community, which those classifications place in tbn; Glottolog's ref 95337 leaves Calvete unassigned among the four Tunebo codes. Glottolog's MED for barr1251, Rivet 1924, is a compilation whose only Casanare-area data are Fabo 1911's Manare wordlist (Manare adjoins Barro Negro on Rivet's map, p. 21); both are silent on stress. Headland 1997 (p. 16, contrastive stress, non-tonal) describes Central Tunebo [tuf] cent2150, not tbn.
